newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Britain to do "utmost" to protect HK legislature.
newsitem.headline: Britain to do "utmost" to protect HK legislature.

text.p: Hong Kong's top civil servant said on Tuesday Britain and Hong Kong would do their utmost to stop Beijing from dissolving the territory's elected legislature after next year's handover of the British colony to China.
Hong Kong Chief Secretary Anson Chan told a business forum in Sydney that Hong Kong needed a credible legislature after the July 1 handover of power.

"Hong Kong needs a credible legislature, one whose members are openly and freely elected and who represent the whole spectrum of political opinion in Hong Kong in order to underpin the rule of law and to ensure a smooth transition," Chan told the business gathering.
Angered by unilateral democratic reforms undertaken by Britain, Beijing has vowed to dissolve Hong Kong's elected Legislative Council after the handover and replace it with a provisional legislature.
Opponents of the move have argued that it would violate the 1984 Sino-British Joint Declaration and Basic Law, which laid down the terms of the transition to Chinese rule.

"I cannot pretend to you that the whole question of the provisional legislature is anything other than difficult," Chan said. "It introduces uncertainty at the very time that the community and the civil service wants reassurance of continuity.

"The British and Hong Kong governments have made our position on this important issue clear to China and we will continue to do our utmost to persuade the Chinese side off this course of action," she said.
Chan, the first ethnic Chinese or woman to hold the chief secretary's post, is heading a delegation of Hong Kong trade officials and business leaders on a week-long visit to Australia.
Hong Kong and Australia have strong trade links, with bilateral trade rising 16 percent last year to A$5.6 billion ($4.42 billion).
Chan said Hong Kong was also Australia's fourth largest source of foreign investment, which stands at around A$14.5 billion and its fourth largest destination for foreign investment at A$2.2 billion.
